items.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
items.content: <article>Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Alexis Christoforous, David Gura, and Christina Ruffini as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Colleges Face a Shrinking Student Pipeline
items.content: <article>US colleges are confronting a prolonged demographic squeeze as the number of high school graduates, after peaking in 2025, is projected to decline 13% through 2041, putting particular pressure on regional schools with limited endowments. Joining David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend is Carleton College Professor of Economics Nathan Grawe who explains that institutions are cutting programs, competing harder for students and emphasizing affordability and return on investment, while inflation-adjusted tuition at public four-year colleges has fallen 7% over the past decade. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Sanctions Target Iran’s Weakened Regional Network
items.content: <article>The US is preparing a new campaign of economic pressure on Iran after diplomacy and months of fighting failed to produce a durable settlement, with President Donald Trump warning countries against maintaining trade ties with Tehran. Atlantic writer and Columbia University Institute of Global Politics Distinguished Fellow Kim Ghattas is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that sanctions remain a blunt tool that will deepen hardship for ordinary Iranians, but Tehran’s weakened regional network and growing economic strain could make the latest pressure campaign different from those of the past 47 years. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Small Dogs, Big Demand as Dachshund Popularity Takes Off
items.content: <article>Dachshunds are enjoying a global popularity boom, climbing to No. 5 in the American Kennel Club’s 2025 rankings as owners embrace their small size and outsized personalities.  The surge is supporting everything from breed meetups to dachshund cafes, even as owners contend with health concerns including intervertebral disc disease, which may affect roughly one in four dachshunds. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss all things Dachshund is Bloomberg News Bangkok Bureau Chief Randy Thanthong-Knight. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Study Shows AI Hitting Paychecks, Not Payrolls
items.content: <article>Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok says early labor-market data suggest AI’s first impact is appearing more in wages than employment. In a study of hundreds of occupations, Slok found that jobs with higher exposure to AI have seen weaker wage growth, while the employment effect remains relatively small. But the picture is still coming into focus: Slok says AI is also helping fuel record business formation, which could create new jobs and make the economy more dynamic. Former IBM HR chief Diane Gherson says companies are already deciding which work can be automated, which employees can be retrained and whether AI savings come through layoffs, slower hiring or reskilling.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Casinos Shift Focus From Gambling to Lure Gen Z With Sports, Dining
items.author: Brianna Sosa
items.content: <article>The new mission for casino operators: Look less like casinos.</article>

items.title: American Whiskey Pays Price for Canada Trade Rift
items.content: <article>US spirits exports to Canada fell 70% from March through December 2025 after most provinces removed American alcohol from their shelves, while exports elsewhere rose 2.5%. American Whiskey Association President & CEO Michael Bilello is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says restoring market access is only the first challenge, American whiskey producers also need to rebuild demand among Canadian consumers after more than a year of trade tensions. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: MI6 Veteran Warns Against Politicizing Intelligence
items.content: <article>Former Head of MI6 Sir Richard Dearlove joins Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the current state of the international intelligence community.  Dearlove says that UK-US intelligence cooperation remains close but expressed concern about politicization and personnel changes inside the CIA, an issue that has also drawn scrutiny amid broader changes across the US intelligence community. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Canada Pushes Back as US Trade Talks Collapse
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News Executive Editor for Canada Derek Decloet joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that Canadians are frustrated but not necessarily surprised after last-minute US-Canada negotiations collapsed, triggering 50% US tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods and a dollar-for-dollar retaliation pledge from Ottawa. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Russia’s Rosatom Returns Workers to Iran’s Bushehr Nuclear Plant
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Russia state-owned atomic energy company Rosatom is continuing to return employees to Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant, Interfax reported, citing the company’s Chief Executive Officer Alexey Likhachev.</article>

items.title: Bond Market Tests Limits of Treasury Intervention
items.content: <article>Joining Bloomberg This Weekend is Bloomberg Radio host of "Masters in Business" Barry Ritholtz and he tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s bond-market moves may provide short-term relief but cannot override persistent inflation, rising debt and the forces setting long-term yields. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: BTW: Headlines You May Have Missed
items.content: <article>LinkedIn becoming a dating site, ghost jobs, fun at home, and farmers saying no to data centers: Alexis Christoforous joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to share headlines from this week that may have gone under the radar. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Chinese AI Models Gain Ground on Price and Use
items.content: <article>Chinese AI models are rapidly narrowing the performance gap with US rivals while gaining users with lower prices and open-weight technology that lets companies deploy them locally. Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Luz Ding is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Chinese AI Models capabilities are approaching leading US models at lower cost. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Keeps Trump Ballroom Work Going
items.content: <article>Chief Justice John Roberts temporarily allowed construction of President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom to continue while the Supreme Court considers whether to grant a longer stay, after lower courts said the project required congressional authorization. Bloomberg News Supreme Court Reporter Greg Stohr joins hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to explain that the court also weighs challenges involving Trump’s mail ballot order and the administration prepares for expected litigation over its new Canada tariffs. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: The AI Spending Spree Comes With a Catch
items.content: <article>Sam Palmisano says the AI boom is built on long-cycle bets in data centers, chips and energy, even as AI software changes at breakneck speed. If adoption slows or cheaper Chinese open-source models gain traction, Big Tech may have to rethink the spending plans behind today’s AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: India’s Foreign Minister to Visit Russia Amid US Tariff Threat
items.author: Mihir Mishra
items.content: <article>India‘s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will visit Russia and co-chair the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission meeting on trade, science, technology, and culture.</article>

items.title: India’s Central Bank Says Forex Deposit Inflows at $65.4 Billion
items.author: Mihir Mishra
items.content: <article>India garnered over $65 billion through special foreign currency deposits from its 35 million-strong diaspora, latest figures from the central bank showed Saturday.</article>

items.title: Mexico Optimistic it Can Achieve Lower US Tariffs on Cars, Steel
items.author: Alex Vasquez
items.content: <article>Mexico’s top trade negotiator expressed optimism he can secure less burdensome tariff terms from the US on Mexican automobile and steel exports, similar to revised measures Washington is discussing with Canada.</article>

items.title: Vingroup Among Vietnam Stocks to Debut on FTSE’s EM Index
items.author: Nguyen Kieu Giang
items.content: <article>Vingroup JSC is among over 100 Vietnamese companies added to FTSE Russell’s Global Equity Indexes late Friday, marking a key step in the country’s long-awaited transition from frontier to secondary emerging market status.</article>
